Append-only record of decisions that shape cross-repo work. Newest first. Reversing a decision gets a **new entry** that supersedes the old one — don't edit history.

Format: context → decision → rationale. Status is **Accepted** unless marked otherwise.

---

## D-010 · Wiki repo hosting namespace — **Open**

*2026-08-17.* The wiki (and the delivery-platform repos) currently live under the `ncsizemore` personal GitHub namespace. Whether to migrate to a team/org namespace is undecided and is coupled to the broader platform org-ownership question (bus-factor mitigation). Until decided, the wiki develops locally / under personal namespace; migration is a rename, not a rewrite, because content is plain markdown in git.

## D-009 · WIP discipline: ≤2 active tracks, no branch older than a week

*2026-08-17.* The Dec 2025 refactor stalled partly because work accumulated on a long-lived branch that drifted 74 commits behind `dev`. Rule: at most two modernization tracks active at once; every increment merges to `dev` (or lands in this wiki) within a session or two; no working branch lives past ~a week.

## D-008 · Toy fixture is the keystone artifact; spike it early

*2026-08-17.* A small, self-contained model specification plus trivial data manager that runs in seconds — no NAS, no multi-GB simsets. It is the shared foundation for the test suite, runnable `@examples`, vignettes, and onboarding. It carries real technical uncertainty (no minimal JHEEM model has ever existed), so it gets a time-boxed spike before anything is scheduled on top of it. Fallback if "truly trivial" proves hard: a pinned, shrunken real workspace (à la `jheem-container-minimal`).

## D-007 · Calibration observability: read-only monitor first, in-loop stop later

*2026-08-17.* Team wants likelihood-progress visibility, per-city mixing stats, and termination of non-mixing cities. `bayesian.simulations` already checkpoints chains (with acceptance counts) to cache directories — so phase 1 is a **read-only monitor** over those caches (traces, acceptance, R-hat/ESS via `posterior`/`coda`), which touches no science path and can ship immediately. Phase 2 — graceful stop via a sentinel file checked at cache writes — modifies the sampling loop and therefore waits until a regression net exists. Monitoring/diagnostics live **above** the engine (analysis layer), never welded into `CALIBRATION_main.R`.

## D-006 · Documentation split: in-repo for API, wiki for cross-repo

*2026-08-17.* jheem2 API documentation (roxygen with runnable `@examples`, vignettes, pkgdown site) lives in the jheem2 repo, versioned with the code and executed by CI. The wiki holds only cross-cutting knowledge (ecosystem map, runbooks, decisions, roadmap). Boundary rule: *changes with a commit → repo; spans repos or outlives commits → wiki.* Corollary: examples are written against the toy fixture and never `\dontrun{}`, so docs double as regression tests.

## D-005 · Wiki: markdown-in-git substrate, rendered site as the team surface

*2026-08-17.* Canonical content is markdown in a git repo; a Quarto-rendered static site (GitHub Pages; later `docs.jheem.org`) is what the team browses. Rejected: GitHub's built-in wiki (hidden secondary repo, no CI/PR review, weak search) and wiki products like Confluence/Notion (breaks the agent-maintained update loop, creates a second source of truth, vendor lock-in). Rationale: readers vastly outnumber writers; the read path gets a real website, the write path stays PR-reviewed plain text that both humans and AI agents can maintain.

## D-004 · Syphilis-manager CI is the data-manager template

*2026-08-17 (direction established by team earlier in 2026).* The syphilis manager's pipeline — immutable release-pinned raw data (`data-raw-v*`), parameterized `jheem2_ref`, hybrid local/CI section builds converging on one regression-gated merge workflow, explicit promotion — is the pattern for all data managers. Next graduates: census and surveillance managers (currently ride along as pre-built dependencies). Long-term: reduce serialized-R6 fragility with a format-versioned data representation.

## D-003 · Structural decomposition of jheem2 is deferred, not canceled

*2026-08-17.* The 5-package split proposed in the Dec 2025 analysis is postponed until after API curation and a real test suite exist. Skepticism recorded about the multi-repo endgame at current team size (coordination cost of 5 versioned packages vs. enforced internal layering in one). The dependency/cycle analysis itself remains valid input; re-verify against current `dev` before acting on it.

## D-002 · Mine the `refactor/extract-packages` branch; don't merge or rebase it

*2026-08-17.* The Dec 2025 refactor branch (jheem.core extraction, "Phase 1 Week 1") is 74+ commits behind `dev`; rebasing a ~5,600-insertion structural change is riskier than redoing it on a tested base. Salvage instead: the architecture/dependency analysis (archived here), the `validate.R` golden-fingerprint concept (seed of the future test suite), and the concrete bug discoveries in its ISSUES.md — unregistered S3 methods, load-time top-level code, tracked `.o` artifacts — which are fixable on `dev` today.

## D-001 · Test-first sequencing for all jheem2 structural work

*2026-08-17.* Characterization/golden-master tests + CI come **before** refactoring, extraction, or engine changes — not "after the architecture stabilizes." This inverts the Dec 2025 execution order, which deferred testthat and stalled. Interim net until in-package tests exist: the `jheem-containers` golden/perturbation suite, run against candidate jheem2 refs (the base image pins jheem2, so the container cascade can gate engine changes now).
